results.notes:
The gateway domain audit_compliance.rs is built and registered. Every route is gated by has_authorized_org_role(owner/admin) on the live membership, and a member gets a typed 403 before any upstream is called.

Compliance routes: GET /api/v1/audit/compliance/{events,manifest,keys,export-status} and POST .../verify, proxied to audit-core /v1/compliance/audit/*. The org comes from authorized_org_id and the role sent in the v3 delegation is the live membership role, not the platform role, because audit-core checks UserRole. Query strings are rebuilt from a per-route allow-list. A client org_id, unknown parameters, blank values and repeated parameters are dropped, and values over 512 bytes get a 400. The verify body keeps only from_seq, from_hash and max_rows, is capped at 4 KiB, and must be a JSON object.

SIEM routes: GET/POST /api/v1/audit/siem-destinations and PATCH/DELETE .../{id}, proxied to org-core /orgs/{org}/siem-destinations[/{id}]. The org is the session's, org_id/orgId are stripped from bodies because org-core refuses unknown fields, the destination id is validated as [A-Za-z0-9_-]{1,64}, and the secret is passed through and never logged. Routes sit behind require_session and rate_limit_middleware. No new switch is added: the routes are admin-gated, and org-core answers 404 until ORG_SIEM_DESTINATIONS_ENABLED=1 (S7).

audit-compliance-client.ts reads the whole envelope because requestJson drops meta, which the event page needs for next_cursor and head_seq. It adds an exportComplianceEvents async generator that follows the cursor. Failures throw the usual typed ApiError.

action-registry.ts gains audit.verify_chain, audit.export_log and audit.create/update/delete_siem_destination. They are human-only: model-eligibility.ts is an allowlist and I did not add them, so the catalog-manifest model-eligible set is unchanged and its test passes.

depth_findings.text: Before AUDIT_SIEM_EXPORT_ENABLED is switched on for any org, the S2 details guard must move from observe to enforce (or the golden content-free check run on live rows): the exporter ships `details` exactly as stored, so a producer that puts content in details would leave the database for a customer SIEM.

Egress guard, signature, ordering, lag alert and dedup are proven only against in-process fakes and httptest TLS servers; the plan's live evidence (real receiver, real org-core destination via gateway, audit-verify over received NDJSON plus head record, lag alert firing and clearing) has not been run.

The exporter connects with the same DATABASE_URL user as audit-core, so it holds write rights on audit_events although it needs only SELECT on the audit tables plus read/write on audit_export_cursors; a dedicated least-privilege role would shrink the blast radius of an SSRF-adjacent bug in the one process that dials customer addresses.

No leader lock: two exporter replicas would each deliver every batch (the receiver dedups on (org_id, chain_seq), cursors never go backwards) but would double the load; compose runs one replica, so only the runbook (S9) needs to say so.

A new destination starts at cursor 0 and exports the entire retained chain; the owner may want a 'from now' option (or an org-core start_from field) for large orgs, which needs a change in org-core's schema and the golden.

audit_export_cursors rows of a deleted destination or an erased org are never pruned (the runner forgets the destination in memory only); tie cursor deletion into the org erasure path or a periodic sweep against org-core's list.

The lag gauge is the worst destination per kind, not per destination (no destination label by design); add a per-destination view through GET /export-status in the Space admin UI, and a rules test that the 15 min lag alert resolves after a drain.

No test covers a receiver that accepts the request but is slow beyond 10 s (timeout code path), or HEC's partial-success 2xx answers (HEC can return 200 with a non-zero code body; the exporter treats any 2xx as success and discards the body).

HEC requests carry no channel or ack header, so delivery is at-least-once without indexer acknowledgement; and the extra `reason` and `org_id` fields on gap markers should be documented in the S9 runbook as part of the export format.

Before AUDIT_SIEM_EXPORT_ENABLED is turned on for any org, the S2 details guard must be enforcing or the export-content-free golden check must run on live rows, because the exporter ships `details` exactly as stored.
The egress guard, HMAC, ordering, dedup and lag alert are proven only against in-process fakes and httptest TLS servers; the plan's live evidence is outstanding.

The exporter connects with the same database role as the audit-core server, so the one process that dials customer addresses holds write rights on audit_events; a dedicated SELECT-plus-cursor role would shrink the blast radius.

There is no leader lock, so two exporter replicas would double-deliver every batch (the receiver dedups on (org_id, chain_seq) and cursors never go backwards); the S9 runbook must state single-replica.
A new destination starts at cursor 0 and exports the whole retained chain; the owner may want a start-from-now option, which needs an org-core schema and golden change.
audit_export_cursors rows of deleted destinations or erased orgs are never pruned; the runner forgets them in memory only.

No test covers a receiver slower than 10 s (the timeout path), HEC partial-success answers (HTTP 200 with a non-zero code body, which the exporter treats as success), or the 15-minute lag alert resolving after a drain.

A destination with an unknown kind calls Cursors.Fail, but audit_export_cursors.kind has a CHECK limited to ndjson_webhook and splunk_hec, so that insert fails and is logged as a cursor_write error with the streak forced to 1; the backoff still applies but the failure is not recorded in the table.

The lag gauge reports the worst destination per kind, not per destination; per-destination detail only comes through GET /export-status. The extra `reason` and `org_id` fields on gap markers belong in the S9 runbook's export format.

results.notes:
The exporter is built and unit-tested with every switch off by default. The slice is partial for two reasons, both shared-file hand-backs: the audit-core migration list (migrate.go, not owned) must list 010, and the compose service in docker-compose.yml (shared) must be added. Until both land, the exporter waits for audit_export_cursors and the export-status route returns 500 query_failed on a real store; it does not return empty. promtool was not available, so the new rules and their unit tests are YAML-checked by eye only.

Design as built. The exporter polls org-core's internal route every 30 s with principal audit-core and scope org:siem:read:any. It drains each enabled destination in chain order: 500 rows per batch, bodies packed under 1 MiB minus an 8 KiB reserve for the closing head record, up to 100 batches per pass. The cursor in audit_export_cursors advances only after a 2xx. Failures back off 5 s doubling to 15 min and are recorded as a fixed-vocabulary code such as http_503, timeout, egress_blocked or redirect_refused. Every batch closes with an audit_chain_head record carrying the newest attestation. A new destination starts at seq 0, so the whole retained chain is exported.

Egress guard. https only, no userinfo, no proxy. DNS is resolved in the dialer, every answer is checked, and the checked IP is dialled, which defeats rebinding. Blocked ranges: loopback, RFC1918, link-local including 169.254.169.254, CGNAT, ULA, multicast, reserved, and IPv4-mapped, NAT64, 6to4 and Teredo forms. No redirects are followed (a 3xx is a failure), the timeout is 10 s, the body cap is 1 MiB, and the response is read to at most 64 KiB and discarded. The Destination type redacts itself under %v, %+v, %#v and JSON, and egress and org-core errors are stripped to a cause so no URL or token reaches a log.

Configuration. AUDIT_SIEM_EXPORT_ENABLED and AUDIT_SIEM_ALLOW_PRIVATE_DESTINATIONS use audit-core's strict parser (only the literal "1" enables). The private-destination switch is a boot failure under ENVIRONMENT=production, even when the exporter is idle. Idle means metrics only.

export-status is now real. complianceExportStatus reads per-destination cursors through an optional ExportStatus interface on the store, with no URL or secret in the response. The existing empty-state test still passes.

Metrics are registered in internal/siem/runner.go: audit_siem_export_lag_seconds{destination_kind}, audit_siem_export_batches_total{result} and audit_siem_destinations{state}. The prometheus scrape job audit-siem-exporter:9091 is added, plus rules ControlAuditSIEMExportLag (more than 15 min for 5 m) and ControlAuditSIEMExportFailing (failure ratio above 0.5 for 10 m), each with unit tests in the rules test file.
